I wrote `SKELETON.md` with a one-line skeleton change.

The change adds one method, `src/packageurl/__init__.py::PackageURL.__hash__(self) -> int`. It hashes the purl string that `to_string()` returns.

`PackageURL` is built on a namedtuple, so its default hash tries to hash every field. One field, `qualifiers`, is a dict (the `OrderedDict` in the error), and dicts can't be hashed. Hashing the purl string avoids that. Two equal `PackageURL`s produce the same string, so they get the same hash, and instances then work in sets and as dict keys.

No other function, type or calling rule needs to change, so I added no other lines.
